NEWS FROM THE BOARD August 2024 NEWS FROM THE BOARD A monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. Tom Dayley - Commissioner Rod Beck - Board Chairman Ryan Davidson - Commissioner HELP ALWAYS AVAILABLE FOR ANYONE EXPERIENCING HOMELESSNESS Ada County Commissioners Tour Next Step Facility on Curtis Road The door is always open, and space is always available at the River of Life Rescue Mission or City Light Home for Women and Children, for anyone experiencing homelessness. Both locations are part of the Boise Rescue Mission Ministries, a local nonprofit organization that helps countless individuals and families navigate homelessness. The organization does not accept any government money. Founded in 1958 the Boise Rescue Mission’s sole purpose is to transform lives for the better. Just this year, 296 individuals have transitioned from homelessness to independent living with the help of skilled case managers. Ada County Commissioners, Rod Beck (Chairman), Ryan Davidson, and Tom Dayley toured the Next Step facility on Curtis Road on August 26th. This former assisted living facility has 58 apartments and serves three meals a day.

# Page 2^page=2
Thank you, Reverend Bill Roscoe, and your welcoming staff, for educating the public on what is available every day to our community’s vulnerable population including families and veterans experiencing homelessness. While the core of the program is bible based, all religious services provided here are 100% voluntary. To learn more about this invaluable community asset including a list of all the facilities available please visit https://boiserm.org/ 2

# Page 3^page=3
DO YOU KNOW ABOUT ALLUMBAUGH HOUSE? Ada County Provides Significant Financial Support to Local Agencies Ada County is proud to support Terry Reilly Health Services and Allumbaugh House by providing important funding each year as part of the county’s budget: More than $253,000 for Terry Reilly Health Services, and more than $330,000 for Allumbaugh House. Both of these organizations have deep roots in the community and do so much to help some of our most vulnerable. Ada County Commissioners Rod Beck (Chairman), Ryan Davidson and Tom Dayley toured Allumbaugh House to see firsthand how this community resource is a literal lifeline for so many. The board was joined by Ada County Paramedics Chief Shawn Rayne and EMS Integration Officer Mark Babson. Allumbaugh House provides short-term medically monitored detoxification and behavioral health crisis services 24/7. The statistics are heartbreaking. 50% of the patients who come to the facility are chronically homeless. 50% have alcohol addiction issues and 40% are struggling to escape from the grips of fentanyl. 70% of the patients have both substance abuse and mental health issues. Ada County is committed to helping to fund this facility along with other important supporters including St. Luke’s, Saint Alphonsus, the State of Idaho through the Department of Health and Welfare, and the cities of Boise, Meridian, Garden City, Kuna and Eagle. Thank you to Heidi Hart, with Terry Reilly Health Services, Deanna Watson with the Boise City Ada County Housing Authority (BCACHA) and Cindy Miller, Director of Substance Use Services at Allumbaugh House, for providing important information on how this particular facility operates. Pictured L-R: Shawn Rayne, Director Ada County Paramedics Heidi Hart, Terry Reilly Health Services Tom Dayley, Ada County Commissioner, Rod Beck, Ada County Commission Chairman Cindy Miller, Director of Substance Use Services Allumbaugh House Mark Babson, EMS Integration Officer Deanna Watson, BCACHA Ryan Davidson, Ada County Commissioner 3

# Page 4^page=4
COMMISSIONERS TOUR ADA COUNTY SHERIFF’S OFFICE TRAINING CENTER The Ada County Sheriff’s Office training facility in Meridian, Idaho has 80 to 100 people a day working inside. The facility serves as a centralized training location for certifications and other essential knowledge needed to perform complex jobs in highly challenging environments. You’ll see everything from classroom instruction to arrest and control techniques in the mat room. Law enforcement personnel also practice hands-on management of various situations they may encounter including low light chaotic scenarios. “It is difficult to describe the importance of training within the law enforcement community. Law enforcement officers have to make split-second decisions, often with little to no information, that put themselves and the community at risk. Officers will rise to the level of their training under stress, punctuating the importance of a consistent, sound training regimen. The loss of Deputy Tobin Bolter in recent months, spotlights the inherent risks of the job and underscores the reason for the need to train as often as we can,” said Lieutenant Dave Moodie, Ada County Sheriff’s Office Training Division. Thank you to Ada County Sheriff Matt Clifford for hosting the Ada County Commissioners on this comprehensive tour. Thank you also to Captain Jared Watson, Sergeant Matt Navest and Lieutenant Dave Moodie for insight on how the facility works. Pictured L-R: Captain Jared Watson, Ada County Commissioner Tom Dayley, Ada County Sheriff Matt Clifford, Sergeant Matt Navest, Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck, Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson, and Lieutenant Dave Moodie 4

5 BOISE BENCH LIONS CLUB LEARNS MORE ABOUT THE PARK AT EXPO IDAHO Thank you to the Boise Bench Lions Club for inviting Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson to speak to the lunch group about one of the most anticipated projects in Ada County! The Park at Expo Idaho will be completed in 2026 and will serve as a wonderful tribute to the open spaces and green areas so many Idahoans cherish. The 55+ acre park, right along the Boise River, will include a world class skate park, playing fields, nature trails and pavilions. Keep track of what’s happening on the Ada County website. https://adacounty.id.gov/commissioners/the- park-at-expo-idaho/ ADA COUNTY GOVERNMENT In addition to elected offices, Ada County government includes thirteen individual departments. Each department provides important services to our residents in Star, Eagle, Meridian, Boise, Garden City, Kuna, and Unincorporated Ada County. These services include law enforcement protection, emergency preparedness, election services, parks and waterways, public defense, indigent services, juvenile court, solid waste management, the Western Idaho Fair, Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement and more. Learn more about the services provided to you by Ada County www.adacounty.id.gov/ 5

# Page 6^page=6
6 ADA COUNTY PARKS & WATERWAYS AND ADA COUNTY COMMISSIONERS UNVEIL NEW IMPROVED SECTION OF GREENBELT PATHWAY Did you know Ada County manages more than eleven miles of the Greenbelt Pathway? Ada County Parks & Waterways Director Scott Koberg, and Garden City Mayor John Evans, joined the Ada County Commissioners on August 5th to unveil a beautifully updated section of Ada County’s Greenbelt. This project was the end result of a lot of hard work and dedication by countless Ada County staff, and so many wonderfully collaborative partners. The 1.64-mile section of this popular stretch is now smoother and wider. This is great news for cyclists, runners, walkers, and everyone else who uses the Greenbelt. The project was completed ahead of schedule and converted a damaged, bumpy, narrow asphalt surface to concrete. The new concrete section is wider and has centerline striping. Thank you to our Greenbelt users for your patience and understanding during this challenging project. We hope you all enjoy this new, wider, safer, smoother section of the Boise River Greenbelt! Pictured L-R: Scott Koberg, Director Ada County Parks & Waterways; Rod Beck, Chairman Ada County Board of Commissioners; Ryan Davidson, Ada County Commissioner and John Evans, Garden City Mayor 6

# Page 7^page=7
EMPLOYEE VOLUNTEERS REPRESENT ADA COUNTY AT THE 2024 WESTERN IDAHO FAIR BOOTH The 2024 Western Idaho Fair is in the books. We heard so many positive things about Ada County and the valuable services we provide to residents and taxpayers throughout the county. For everyone who volunteered to staff the Ada County Booth – Thank you! You’re what makes the county such a great place to work! Thank you Bob Batista and Kelly Sarich for giving those who volunteered two free tickets! Much Appreciated! The most overheard comments were excitement and appreciation about The Park at Expo Idaho. We were overjoyed to hear so many people say they’d heard about it already. We were also excited to tell them it would be completed in 2026. Thank you to the Ada County Assessor’s Office for providing great information on property tax reduction programs and other services so many people count on. Thank you also to Ada County Elections for helping folks register to vote! Almost every Ada County department and elected office had smiling and knowledgeable volunteers at the booth. It was great to spend time with co-workers from other areas of county government. We are happy to report that next year we will be teaming up with the Ada County Sheriff’s Office, so we are all in the same area! See you next year at the Western Idaho Fair! 7

DON WATTS – 20 YEARS Thank you, Don Watts, for 20 years with Ada County! Don started with the county as a temporary employee in June 2004 and within a few months he had worked his way into a full time Land Records Tech position. The Ada County Assessor’s Office is very fortunate to have recruited Don. Twenty years ago, prior to coming to Ada County, he gained his experience with an engineering firm of 5 years as a draftsman and another 5 years as survey crew chief. Within a few years he was again promoted to Land Records Analyst and then in 2017 he became part of the management team. Under his guidance and management, he has updated the department’s policies and procedures, and has identified efficiencies that allow Land Records to create more parcels and process more ownership changes with fewer staff. In just 2023 alone, Don and his staff created nearly 5,000 new parcels and processed nearly 22,000 deeds. He is never satisfied with the status-quo, and his passion for the work and meticulous approach make our office better. More importantly, his leadership benefits the taxpayers of Ada County and promotes responsible and responsive government. The Assessor’s Office is extremely grateful to have Don on our team and we commend him for his years of service ERIC HUSKEY - 20 YEARS Congratulations to Eric Huskey for twenty years of outstanding service with Ada County Paramedics. Eric is such a trooper he showed up bright and early for his employee recognition certificate after pulling a 24-hour shift! Eric’s start with Ada County Paramedics twenty years ago marked a bright spot in the history of the organization. Over those many years, Eric’s knowledge, willingness to learn, and ability to patiently teach benefited countless paramedics and EMTs. Eric continues to do that with a smile and a caring approach. Shortly after being hired, Eric became a Field Training Officer. Just after that, Eric became a member of Ada County Paramedic’s Tactical Medical Team, a team focused on supporting law enforcement. He also became a member of the Special Operations Team, a team focused on rope rescue. In both roles, Eric’s contribution was significant. Several years ago, Eric became a Field Captain. All that knowledge and experience led Eric, deservedly so, to his current role as Battalion Chief. In this role, Eric very capably leads a shift of Paramedics and EMTs as they respond to 911 calls. The role of Battalion Chief is a difficult, demanding job that Eric handles well. Thank you for all you do Eric. 9
